anchors.1: Explicit categorical refusal for this concern even under any stated modification; never infer from current-route rejection alone.
anchors.2: Strong personal boundary with very limited tolerance; may accept only if the intrusive effect is removed or avoided. Conditional openness does not erase the boundary.
anchors.3: Strong concrete disruption objection; accepts only after substantial mitigation, removal or avoidance of that effect.
anchors.4: Localized intrusion/reservation with conditional openness requiring a meaningful change.
anchors.5: Balanced concern-specific willingness and reservations; uncertainty without a position stays null.
anchors.6: Cautious acceptance with limited reservations and willingness to tolerate some impact; NOT merely accepting after an intolerable effect is eliminated.
anchors.7: Qualified acceptance with manageable reservations or conditions, tolerating some impact rather than requiring elimination of a strong boundary.
anchors.8: Clear concern-specific support, including medical-public-service welfare support; other concern opposition is separate.
anchors.9: Explicit unqualified endorsement of the assessed concern facet; no inferred global readiness.

index_interpretation: Illustrative arithmetic index over ordinal concern scores; not a calibrated measurement.
bottleneck_rationale: Experimental generalization of FN p.7 minimum privacy score 2 plus 2: eligible assessed phase-1 scores <=3, minimum plus 2. No claim FN establishes a universal threshold or offset.
